nodes.title: Read the data flow
nodes.summary: Section 1: CSV in, SQLite table out, one query to check. No files change. Done when you can name the table the loader creates.

verification.prompt: Name the table the loader creates and the file it reads.

nodes.title: Write the CSV
nodes.summary: Section 2: write data.csv with three rows. Done when the file exists.
commands:
cat > data.csv <<'EOF'
name,qty
apple,3
pear,5
plum,7
EOF

nodes.title: Write the loader script
nodes.summary: Section 3: load.py reads data.csv into data.db. Sibling of 2-write-csv.
commands:
cat > load.py <<'EOF'
import csv
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect('data.db')
conn.execute('DROP TABLE IF EXISTS items')
conn.execute('CREATE TABLE items (name TEXT, qty INTEGER)')
with open('data.csv') as f:
    rows = [(r['name'], int(r['qty'])) for r in csv.DictReader(f)]
conn.executemany('INSERT INTO items VALUES (?, ?)', rows)
conn.commit()
conn.close()
EOF

nodes.title: Load the CSV into data.db
nodes.summary: Section 4: run load.py, then count the rows. Joins the CSV and script branches. Done when the count prints 3.

nodes.title: Query the table
nodes.summary: Section 5: list the names in order. Done when the output has apple, pear, plum on separate lines.
commands: python3 -c "import sqlite3; [print(r[0]) for r in sqlite3.connect('data.db').execute('select name from items order by name')]"

verification.command: python3 -c "import sqlite3; [print(r[0]) for r in sqlite3.connect('data.db').execute('select name from items order by name')]"

nodes.title: Note where the backup lives
nodes.summary: Section 6: a manual step outside the workspace. Done when you have recorded where you keep copies of data.db.

verification.prompt: Confirm you noted where a copy of data.db is kept.
